name: University of Sheffield
notes: One university-wide minimum for both levels. Some academic departments require a higher score.

name: University of Sussex
notes: Courses map to one of three levels: Standard 6.0 (5.5 each), High 6.5 (6.0 each), Advanced 7.0 (6.5 each). The figure shown is the High level, which most courses use.

name: University of Manchester
notes: No single university-wide minimum. Each course sets its own requirement between 5.5 and 7.5, and sub-skill minimums may apply. Check the course profile before applying.

name: University of Warwick
notes: Three published bands: Band A 6.0 (5.5 each), Band B 6.5 (6.0 each), Band C 7.0 (6.5 each). The figure shown is Band B. Your course page names its band. Warwick requires all four scores from one sitting and does not accept the One Skill Retake.

name: University of Bristol
notes: Bristol publishes lettered profiles rather than one minimum. Verified: Profile A 7.5 (7.0 each), Profile B 7.0 (undergraduate needs 7.0 writing and 6.5 elsewhere; postgraduate 6.5 each), Profile E 6.5 (6.0 each). The figure shown is Profile E. Your course page names its profile — check it before applying.

name: University of Leeds
notes: Baseline is 6.0 (5.5 each) for undergraduate degrees and 6.5 (6.0 each) for masters. Leeds states some courses sit higher, so confirm on the course page. Results must be under two years old at course start.

name: King's College London
notes: King's sets a lettered band per course. Undergraduate: Band A 7.5 (7.0 each), Band B 7.0 (6.5 each), Band D 6.5 (6.0 each). Postgraduate: Band B 7.0 (6.5 each), Band C 7.0 (6.5 reading and writing, 6.0 listening and speaking), Band D 6.5 (6.0 each). The figure shown is Band D. All four skills must come from one test.

name: University of Birmingham
notes: Undergraduate courses sit in one of four groups: A 6.0 (5.5 each), B 6.5 (6.0 each), C 7.0 (6.5 each), D 7.0 (7.0 each). The figure shown is Group A. Business School courses in Group B additionally need 6.5 in writing and speaking. Postgraduate figures are published separately and are not covered here.

name: Queen Mary University of London
notes: Requirements are set per school on a numbered band scale. Undergraduate: Band 3 is 6.0 (5.5 each) for Engineering/Science/Maths schools, Band 4 is 6.5 (6.0 each) for Business/Economics, Band 5 is 7.0 (6.0 each) for Arts and health-related institutes. Postgraduate mostly sits at Band 4, with Band 5 for Arts and research programmes. Law has non-standard requirements set separately.

name: Newcastle University
notes: The typical undergraduate baseline is 6.5 overall with no less than 5.5 in each of the four skills; individual course pages state a higher figure where one applies. Postgraduate requirements are set per course rather than centrally and are not covered here.

name: Cardiff University
notes: One university-wide minimum of 6.5 overall with no less than 5.5 in each subskill, published separately but identically for undergraduate and postgraduate applicants. Some courses set a higher requirement — check the course page.

name: University College London (UCL)
notes: UCL runs five numbered levels, identical structure for undergraduate and postgraduate: Level 1 is 6.5 (6.0 each), Level 2 is 7.0 (6.5 each), Level 3 is 7.0 (7.0 each), Level 4 is 7.5 (7.0 each), Level 5 is 8.0 (8.0 each). The figure shown is Level 1, the most common. Your course page names its level.

name: Imperial College London (Business School)
notes: Figure covers Imperial College Business School's postgraduate programmes only, not Imperial's other faculties, which set their own English requirements per department. All four scores must come from one sitting.

name: University of Nottingham
notes: University-wide floor is 6.0 with no less than 5.5 in any element, the same for undergraduate and postgraduate — but Nottingham states many schools and departments require a higher level than this floor, so check the specific course listing.

name: University of Liverpool
notes: Undergraduate floor is 6.0 with no component below 5.5, rising to 7.5 for some clinical courses. Postgraduate taught (master's) programmes ask 6.5 with no component below 6.0; postgraduate research asks the same or 6.5/5.5 depending on department.

name: University of Aberdeen
notes: Undergraduate entry asks 6.0 overall with listening, reading and speaking each at 5.5 but writing specifically at 6.0 — a higher floor on writing alone, not a blanket minComponent. Medicine (MBChB) sits higher. Postgraduate runs two separate tiers (Standard/Higher) set per subject and is not covered here.

name: University of Bath
notes: Bath publishes three postgraduate-taught tiers: Standard 6.5 (6.0 each), Higher 7.0 (6.5 each), Highest 7.0 (7.0 each). The figure shown is Standard, the most common. Undergraduate figures are published separately and are not covered here.

name: University of Reading
notes: Reading's normal postgraduate-taught requirement is 7.0 with no element below 6.0; some courses instead ask the lower alternative of 6.5 with no element below 5.5. Undergraduate figures vary widely by course (from 6.5 up to 8.0 for Speech and Language Therapy) and are not consolidated here.

name: Loughborough University
notes: One university-wide standard of 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each element, applied identically to undergraduate and postgraduate taught degrees. Some Schools set a higher figure, and postgraduate research can ask more depending on the department.

name: University of Hull
notes: Baseline for most courses is 6.0 overall with 5.5 in each of reading, writing, speaking and listening. Hull states some courses need a higher score, and all four skills must come from one test sitting — scores cannot be combined across tests.

name: Royal Holloway, University of London
notes: Undergraduate baseline is 6.5 with no subscore below 5.5, though humanities and business courses specifically ask 6.0 in writing. Taught master's programmes ask 6.5 with no subscore below 6.0; research degrees ask 6.5 overall with writing at 7.0.

name: University of Portsmouth
notes: Most bachelor's degrees ask 6.0 with no component below 5.5. Most master's degrees ask between 6.5 and 7.0 with no component below 6.0 — the figure shown is the lower end of that published range.

name: University of East Anglia (UEA)
notes: Typical undergraduate entry is 6.5 with no less than 5.5 in each component, though some subjects (Literature, Drama and Creative Writing, Chemistry, Pharmacy) need 6.5 in each component instead. Postgraduate research in Social Sciences asks 7.0 with 6.5 in each component; other postgraduate courses vary between 6.5 and 7.0.

name: Lancaster University
notes: Standard undergraduate baseline is 6.5 overall with no element below 5.5. Medicine and Surgery is far higher at 7.0 with no component below 7.0 — a search engine summary conflated this Medicine figure with the general entry standard, which is not correct. Some Science, Mathematics and Social Work courses also sit above the baseline.

name: University of Westminster
notes: Undergraduate baseline is 6.0 with no component below 5.5. Postgraduate baseline is 6.5 overall with writing specifically at 6.0 and other components at least 5.5. Law School and English Literature/Language postgraduate courses ask for 7.0 with 6.5 in each component instead.

name: Sheffield Hallam University
notes: Standard undergraduate requirement is 6.0 with 5.5 in each of listening, speaking, reading and writing. Nursing sits much higher at 7.0 with 6.5 in writing and 7.0 in the other three skills. PhD entry requires 7.0 across every skill. Course pages give the exact figure per course.

name: Oxford Brookes University
notes: Standard undergraduate entry is 6.0 overall with reading and writing each at 6.0 but listening and speaking only at 5.5 — the productive academic skills sit above the receptive ones rather than one flat floor. Law, Architecture, Interior Architecture, English Literature and Health & Social Care courses ask for more. Postgraduate figures are set per course and are not consolidated here.

name: Ulster University
notes: Most courses ask for 6.0 overall with no band under 5.5, the same figure for undergraduate and postgraduate. Some courses set a higher requirement — check the specific course page.

name: Bournemouth University
notes: Bachelor's and taught master's programmes ask for 6.0 overall with no component below 5.5; research degrees (PhD) ask for 6.5 overall with the same 5.5 floor. Some courses set higher figures — check the specific course page.

name: Kingston University
notes: Undergraduate baseline is 6.0 with 5.5 in each element. Postgraduate baseline is 6.5 with 5.5 in each element, though some faculties ask for no element below 6.0 instead.

name: University of Essex
notes: Undergraduate baseline is 6.0 with 5.5 in each component. Postgraduate baseline is 6.5 overall with writing specifically at 6.0 and the remaining components at 5.5. Essex accepts English qualifications up to five years old rather than the more common two-year window.

name: Keele University
notes: Standard undergraduate requirement is 6.0 with 5.5 in every component. Nursing sits far higher: 7.0 overall with 6.5 in writing and 7.0 in the other three skills.

name: University of Stirling
notes: Baseline for most undergraduate and postgraduate taught courses is 6.0 with no sub-skill below 5.5. Some postgraduate programmes (e.g. TESOL) ask for higher, uneven floors across skills instead.

name: University of Greenwich
notes: Postgraduate research figure covers most faculties: 6.5 overall with 6.0 in every element. Greenwich Business School, Education, Health & Human Sciences, and Law, Arts & Social Sciences ask for the stricter 6.5 with 6.5 in every element instead. Undergraduate figures are set per course and are not consolidated here.
